The minimum age to obtain a gun permit depends on the type of permit and jurisdiction. In Pennsylvania, the official standard is that a person must be at least 21 years of age to apply for a License to Carry Firearms (concealed carry) [d8][d7]. However, the Pennsylvania State Police website also notes that persons 18 years of age or older who are licensed to hunt, trap, or fish may apply for a Sportsman's Firearm Permit, which allows carrying a firearm during lawful hunting and related activities [d8]. At the federal level, the law requires a person to be 21 to purchase a handgun from a licensed firearm dealer, and only 18 to purchase a long gun from a dealer [d3]. In Erie County, New York, applicants for a pistol permit must be at least 21 years of age and a county resident [d5]. Additionally, a court ruling in Pennsylvania has allowed otherwise qualified 18-to-20-year-olds to apply for and obtain a License to Carry Firearms in that state [d4], though the official Pennsylvania State Police guidance still cites 21 as the standard age [d8].
